subject: DPA negotiation: audit rights, subprocessors, and docuSign flow
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@healthbridge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, HealthBridge Legal <data-procurement@healthbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA + audit scope for Redwood platform

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — HealthBridge is moving fast and we want to make sure the contract and data controls are aligned before procurement can complete. Attached is our DPA template and a short questionnaire that procurement uses to verify audit scope and third-party controls (HB_DPA_Template_2026.xlsx).

Two quick asks to unblock on our side:
- Can you confirm Redwood's list of subprocessors and whether any processing happens outside the US (we're particularly focused on EU transfers and any APAC backups)?
- Our security team requires either (a) Redwood's latest SOC 2 report + pen test summary, or (b) an agreed remote evidence review. Which is easier for you?
- We usually require audit rights in the DPA for a third-party auditor once per 12 months and limited to incidents. Can you confirm Redwood's posture here or propose wording?

If we can get the DPA ready for e-sign by next week that would let us include Redwood in the July onboarding wave. Please loop in your legal contact and attach any redlines.

Elena
Elena Martinez
Lead, Vendor Risk & Procurement | HealthBridge
elena.martinez@healthbridge.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: HB_DPA_Template_2026.xlsx
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA + audit scope for Redwood platform

Elena — thanks for sharing and for clear asks. Looping in our legal lead, Laura, and privacy/controls owner Karthik.

Quick answers up front:
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessors export (redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.csv). All production processing is in US regions for your account unless otherwise requested; we use EU regions for EU customer tenants on request and apply SCCs or equivalent transfers where applicable.
- Evidence: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II 2025 report and a consolidated pen test executive summary (I can attach once I confirm with Security). If HealthBridge requires a live/remote evidence review instead, we can accommodate via a shared Drive folder and a one-hour walkthrough.
- Audit rights: Redwood's standard is to provide attestations (SOC 2) and a right to commission an independent third-party audit only in cases of material incident or regulatory requirement. We typically limit on-site audits due to customer/other tenant privacy. Laura will propose specific contract language.

I've attached an initial redline of your DPA with our suggested changes (Redwood_DPA_SOFIA_redlines.docx). To keep momentum, I've started a DocuSign envelope that would execute our counterparty DPA when you're ready: https://docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-12345

Next steps we propose:
1) HealthBridge to review our redlines and confirm whether remote evidence + SOC2 is sufficient, or whether you require on-site access.
2) If SOC2 + pen test summary acceptable, we exchange those artifacts and proceed to sign via DocuSign.
3) If HealthBridge wants a limited auditor right, Laura will share alternative language that restricts frequency and scope.

Happy to jump on a short call if helpful — can do tomorrow afternoon PST.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_SOFIA_redlines.docx, redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.csv
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@healthbridge.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA + audit scope for Redwood platform

Elena/Sofia — thanks, reviewing the redline now. A few legal-control points we typically insist on; proposing compact language to keep execution fast:

1) Audit rights scope: we can agree to provide reasonable evidence (SOC 2 report + pen test executive summary) and a remote evidence review once per 12 months. We will not permit broad, unrestricted on-site audits. Proposed clause: "Customer may request a third-party audit only upon a material security incident or where required by applicable law; such audit shall be limited to Redwood's controls relevant to Customer's data and conducted remotely unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current list and notify HealthBridge 30 days prior to adding any subprocessor that could materially impact data transfer locations. We also accept a standard objection process (HealthBridge may object on reasonable grounds).

3) Data transfers: SCCs (or EU adequacy mechanisms) will be applied for EU-to-US transfers. Please confirm if HealthBridge requires a fully EU-hosted tenant rather than SCCs for your use-case.

4) Pen test artifacts: we can provide a high-level summary (scope, critical/important findings, remediation status). We cannot provide raw test output or attacker tool logs. If you require deeper detail, we can propose a scoped NDA and limited preview session.

I attached a short PDF with redline comments (Redwood_DPA_Markup_LB.pdf) — the core ask for HealthBridge is to accept SOC2 + pen test summary and accept SCCs for transfers; for audit rights we'll accept remote evidence + limited third-party audit language.

If HealthBridge can confirm those items today, Sofia can finalize DocuSign and we can move to signature.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Markup_LB.pdf
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@healthbridge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA + audit scope for Redwood platform

Team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear options. HealthBridge is comfortable with the approach below:
- Acceptance: SOC 2 Type II 2025 + pen test executive summary acceptable as primary evidence.
- Transfers: SCCs are acceptable for EU->US transfers; we do not require a fully EU-hosted tenant for the initial agreement.
- Audit rights: we accept the remote-evidence-first approach and will reserve third-party on-site audits only for material incidents. We have no immediate objections to the redline language Laura proposed.

I've uploaded our signed procurement cover page to the Drive link and attached the SOC2 and pen test summary for your records. We will sign the final DPA in DocuSign once you upload the counter-signed envelope.

DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-12345
Drive evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/EXAMPLE-HealthBridge-Evidence

Attachments: HealthBridge_SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf, HealthBridge_PenTest_Summary_2025.pdf

Thanks — Elena
